author: michae2
body:
**sql: bring back resultRowBuffer in updateRun and deleteRun**

For some reason, updateRun and deleteRun differ from insertRun in that
they were creating result slices for RETURNING in processSourceRow,
instead of creating a resultRowBuffer in startExec. This commit does a
small refactor to move allocation of resultRowBuffer to startExec.

This refactor will make it easier for the new UPDATE and DELETE fast
path planNodes to share updateRun and deleteRun with the existing
updateNode and deleteNode.

Epic: None

Release note: None
    
---

**sql: move processSourceRow to updateRun, upsertRun, and deleteRun**

Refactor processSourceRow so that it's a method of updateRun, upsertRun,
and deleteRun, rather than a method of updateNode, upsertNode, and
deleteNode, respectively. This matches insertRun.

This refactor will make it easier for the new UPDATE and DELETE fast
path planNodes to share updateRun and deleteRun with the existing
updateNode and deleteNode. (There's no new fast path in the works for
UPSERT, at least not yet, but upsertRun is changed for completeness.)

Epic: None

Release note: None

author: backspace
body:
This updates code mode to include `clientRequestId` in `POST` requests produced by the editor saving changes. This should prevent some instances of data loss like that seen here:

![screencast 2025-04-08 09-29-30](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/122343a8-4366-4a02-8b4e-f977cbdca5f9)

`clientRequestId` is now prefixed based on the operation that prompted the request. If the user was editing the source, it’s `editor:`. There are other prefixes for different triggering events, like `bot-patch:`, so handlers that receive realm events can decide how to act. This may be improved in the future by being separated instead of prefixed so it can use typing.

I did have assertions that source saves included `clientRequestId` but I removed them in 6b0bc14 as it seemed superficial to me. When the `clientRequestId` lacked a prefix, the `card instance change made in monaco editor is auto-saved` test [failed](https://github.com/cardstack/boxel/runs/40200702549). There’s a corresponding Matrix test included here showing that a change made via editing a card preview is reflected in the source, but it’s skipped because there’s a caching problem preventing the invalidation-prompted refetch from getting the updated source.

An earlier iteration of this PR included the removal of debounce code within the Monaco modifier related to server echoes, which seems like it should entirely be taken care of at the `clientRequestId` level. Unfortunately it [broke](https://github.com/cardstack/boxel/runs/40600832970) a cursor position test and I was unable to figure it out in time.

enable the use of `byref` consistently across all languages.

Co-authored-by: Matt Arsenault <Matthew.Arsenault@amd.com>

Fixes SWDEV-247226.

author: cobalt-github-releaser-bot
body:
Refer to the original PR: https://github.com/youtube/cobalt/pull/5319

When the application is suspended, StarboardBridge clears its ActivityHolder() [here](https://source.corp.google.com/h/lbshell-internal/cobalt_src/+/main:cobalt/android/apk/app/src/main/java/dev/cobalt/coat/StarboardBridge.java;l=175-177;bpv=1;bpt=0;drc=a17da04e52532e5a0480393bc751306db09e97e6). A timing issue arises if openCobaltService () is called [here](https://source.corp.google.com/h/lbshell-internal/cobalt_src/+/main:cobalt/android/apk/app/src/main/java/dev/cobalt/coat/StarboardBridge.java;l=673-676;drc=a17da04e52532e5a0480393bc751306db09e97e6;bpv=1;bpt=0) concurrently, as it may retrieve a null activity from the cleared holder. This causes subsequent asynchronous communication from the platform service to fail, because its callback needs a non-null activity [here](https://source.corp.google.com/h/lbshell-internal/cobalt_src/+/main:cobalt/android/apk/app/src/main/java/dev/cobalt/coat/CobaltService.java;l=100;bpv=1;bpt=0;drc=424d60be6465ceec41b2bcda7b94eaad7539dbb9) to find the shell's webContents().

To fix this, the activity is now explicitly passed into H5vccPlatformService and subsequently forwarded as a parameter to StarboardBridge.openPlatformService(). This ensures the required activity reference is available directly when needed, bypassing the potentially null ActivityHolder and preventing the communication failure.

author: alextwoods
body:
Fix issue in generating event shapes shared between multiple eventstreams by introducing new `SdkEventType` interface.

## Motivation and Context
Currently in Java 2.x, we generate an interface for each eventstream shape. The interface contains an `EventType` enum and an `sdkEventType` method. Values in `EventType` map to the event members in the eventstream, and classes that implement the interface return the appropriate value from `sdkEventType` to signify which event they are. When an event shape is shared between multiple eventstreams it will implement the interface for each eventstream, which leads to incompatible type signatures on the `sdkEventType` method.

## Modifications
1. Introduces a new `SdkEventType` interface that all `EventType` enums implement.
2. The base event POJO defines `sdkEventType` method that returns the new `SdkEventType`. Specific implementations of the event are unchanged and still return the Evenstream specific `EventType`.

## Testing
* Existing eventstream codegen test cases (require minor updates, see updated test code)
* New codegen shared evenstream tests (see model updates in /sharedstream/service-2.json)
* Manually run codgeneration for internal test case model that motivated change.

author: poulok
body:
**Description**:
This PR updates the Event Creator component so that it does not use the serialized generation value stored in the Event Descriptor. Instead, it will use a locally calculated generation called Non-Deterministic Generation, or nGen.

Prior to this PR, several of the classes that implement the tipset event creation algorithm treated self events the same as all other events because generation was available in all events at all times, even at the moment of creation. NGen is assigned by the Orphan Buffer and is not available to the Event Creator when creating new events.

This PR updates the event creator classes to treat self events differently in specific ways, because generation for self events is not required by the tipset algorithm. Tipset advancement via self events does not matter, so nGen for self events is not needed. The PR updates the classes to make this fact clear and handle self events (without an nGen value) accordingly.

Additional Changes:
1. The event creator classes now use `PlatformEvent` instead of `EventDescriptorWrapper` because the former is where `nGen` is set and available.
2. The event creator now signs the events it creates so that it returns instances of `PlatformEvent` instead of `UnsignedEvent`. It didn't make any sense to keep the event signer as a separate component because it was so simple and is configured as a direct component, which means it always runs on the thread as the caller. Plus, this change made the tests easier to update.

**Related issue(s)**:
Fixes #12028

**Notes for reviewer**:
Please pay special attention to the unit tests in this PR. If any are confusing or it is not immediately clear what the do and exactly what they test, I want to improve it.

author: klkvr
body:
Adds logic for pausing/unpausing signers if balance reaches certain values. Current implementation will pause the signer if it can't afford spending 30M gas per the current gas price estimate. This should be a reasonable bound enough to process any pending transactions that may be still in progress.

Balance metrics are still emitted separately by `BalanceCollector`. I'm not sure if we should move this logic into `Signer` and remove the `BalanceCollector` as I assume we might also want to emit metrics for token balances which don't really belong to signer as it doesn't know about tokens that we support.

So imo if we want to collect and record both native and tokens balances those should happen in a separate `BalanceCollector`, otherwise if we just need metric for native balance it's fine to remove `BalanceCollector` and do it directly in `Signer` future.

I've also added tracing spans for all of the signers

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
PR #24429: Fixed failing NCCL Group test on internal CI

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/24429

Previously, this test was failing with 

```
INTERNAL: NCCL operation ncclRecv( recv_buffer.opaque(), ToNcclCount(dtype, count), nccl_dtype, source_rank->value(), comm_, se::gpu::AsGpuStreamValue(stream)) failed: invalid argument (run with NCCL_DEBUG=WARN for details). Last NCCL warning(error) log entry (may be unrelated) 'Recv : invalid root 3 (root should be in the 0..1 range)'.
```

This was because of a mix of the bad channel ids and this missing `replica_count` attribute.

Copybara import of the project:

--
f904b6c985db68ebb2d98f8e8a2a4d2da45834e5 by chaserileyroberts <chaser@nvidia.com>:

Set replica_count=4, removed channel_ids

--
67702da461c3f9bac803cfb01bf9352fec46c610 by chaser <chaser@nvidia.com>:

replica_count -> num_partitions

Merging this change closes #24429
